details: Uses periods of Thousands, Lakhs (1,00,000 = 10^5), and Crores (1,00,00,000 = 10^7).
Commas are placed after 3 digits from the right, and then after every 2 digits (e.g., 1,00,00,000).
evidence_or_examples: Patna's population is 25 Lakhs (25,00,000); Mumbai's population is 2 Crores (2,00,00,000).

details: Uses periods of Thousands, Millions (1,000,000 = 10^6), and Billions (1,000,000,000 = 10^9).
Commas are placed every 3 digits from right to left (e.g., 1,000,000,000).
evidence_or_examples: 1 Million = 10 Lakhs; 1 Crore = 10 Millions; 1 Billion = 100 Crores.

details: To multiply an even number N by 5, halve the number and multiply by 10: N * 5 = (N / 2) * 10.
To multiply a multiple of 4 N by 25, divide by 4 and multiply by 100: N * 25 = (N / 4) * 100.
Single-digit numbers (1-9) consume 9 total positions.
Two-digit numbers (10-99, total 90 numbers) consume 180 total positions (cumulative 189 digits).
Three-digit numbers (100-999, total 900 numbers) consume 2700 positions.
evidence_or_examples: Finding the 100th digit: 100 - 9 = 91 digits from 2-digit numbers. 91 / 2 = 45 with remainder 1. 9 + 45 = 54. Next number is 55, whose first digit is 5.

details: An expression combines numbers and operational signs (+, -, *, /).
Addition (+) and subtraction (-) signs partition expressions into individual terms evaluated prior to final summation.
evidence_or_examples: In 39 - 2 * 6 + 11, evaluate term 2 * 6 = 12 first, giving 39 - 12 + 11 = 38.

details: Brackets group sub-expressions into single compound terms to explicitly mandate evaluation priority.
evidence_or_examples: Queen Alia's coin gift: (100 * 2) + (100 / 2) = 200 + 50 = 250 gold coins.

details: Commutative Addition: a + b = b + a.
Associative Addition: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).
Multiplication distributes over addition: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c.
evidence_or_examples: Melvin's story reading: 8 * (7 - 2) = 8*7 - 8*2 = 56 - 16 = 40 stories.

details: Subtracting a number is equivalent to adding its negative counterpart: a - b = a + (-b).
Removing brackets preceded by a minus sign reverses every internal term's sign: -(a + b) = -a - b and -(a - b) = -a + b.
evidence_or_examples: 18 - 10 = 18 + (-10) = 8; Token model combining 18 blue (+1) and 10 red (-1) tokens leaves 8 blue tokens.

details: Tenth = 1/10 = 0.1; Hundredth = 1/100 = 0.01; Thousandth = 1/1000 = 0.001.
The decimal point separates whole units on the left from fractional place values on the right.
evidence_or_examples: 3.47 = 3 ones + 4 tenths + 7 hundredths = 3 + 4/10 + 7/100.

details: Currency: 1 Rupee = 100 Paise => 1 Paise = ₹0.01 (e.g., 45 p = ₹0.45).
Length: 1 cm = 10 mm => 1 mm = 0.1 cm (e.g., 3 mm = 0.3 cm); 1 m = 1000 mm => 1 mm = 0.001 m.
evidence_or_examples: Honeybee body length: Head 2.3 cm + Thorax 5.4 cm + Abdomen 7.5 cm = 15.2 cm total.

details: Appending trailing zeros to decimal places preserves value (0.2 = 0.20 = 0.200).
Adding and subtracting decimals requires vertical alignment of decimal points so matching place values are operated together.
evidence_or_examples: Comparing 0.2 and 0.09: 0.2 has 2 tenths while 0.09 has 0 tenths, so 0.2 > 0.09.
Fish length difference: Celestial Pearl Danio (2.4 cm) - Philippine Goby (0.9 cm) = 1.5 cm.

details: A letter-number (variable) represents an unspecified, changing numerical value.
Perimeter formulas for regular polygons: Equilateral Triangle = 3s, Square = 4s, Regular Pentagon = 5s, Regular Hexagon = 6s.
evidence_or_examples: Shabnam's age s in terms of Aftab's age a: s = a + 3.

details: Like terms contain identical variables (e.g., 5y and 2y) and combine via numerical coefficients: 5y + 2y = 7y.
Unlike terms (e.g., 3x and 4y) cannot be merged.
evidence_or_examples: Simplify: 5y + x + x + 5y - 6 + 2 = 10y + 2x - 4.

sub_branches.concept: Matchstick Square and Endless Grid Rules
details: Matchstick squares rule: w connected squares require 3w + 1 matchsticks.
Endless 4-column grid rule: Number in row r, column c is given by N = 4(r - 1) + c = 4r - 4 + c.
evidence_or_examples: For 10 squares: 3(10) + 1 = 31 matchsticks.
Location of 143 in 4-column grid: 143 = 4 * 35 + 3 => Column 3, Row 36.

sub_branches.concept: Vertically Opposite Angles and Linear Pairs
details: Two straight lines intersect at at most one unique point, forming four angles.
Vertically opposite angles are equal: angle a = angle c and angle b = angle d.
Linear pairs on a straight line are supplementary: angle a + angle b = 180°.
evidence_or_examples: If intersecting angle a = 35°, adjacent angle b = 180° - 35° = 145°, vertically opposite angle c = 35°, angle d = 145°.

details: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never meet, maintaining constant perpendicular distance throughout.
Perpendicular lines intersect at right angles (90°).
evidence_or_examples: Opposite edges of a ruler, railway tracks.

details: Successive parallel horizontal paper folds produce parallel line creases.
A perpendicular vertical fold across horizontal creases generates right angles.
evidence_or_examples: Folding square paper in half repeatedly creates parallel grid line creases.

details: Children in line report the count of individuals standing ahead who are strictly taller.
Callout numbers uniquely constrain and determine relative height sequence order.
evidence_or_examples: Callout sequence (0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 3) uniquely reconstructs 7 stick figures by height.

details: Even = 2n; Odd = 2n - 1.
Addition: Even + Even = Even; Odd + Odd = Even; Even + Odd = Odd.
Multiplication: Even * Anything = Even; Odd * Odd = Odd.
Page sum on any single loose leaf from a book (2k-1 + 2k = 4k - 1) is always ODD.
evidence_or_examples: Sum of 50 odd numbers is always EVEN.

details: An n x n grid filled with distinct integers where every row, column, and diagonal sums to the same constant.
For digits 1 to 9: Magic Constant S = 15; Center cell x = S / 3 = 5.
Exactly 8 unique magic squares exist via rotation/reflection.
evidence_or_examples: Standard magic square row 1: [8, 1, 6], row 2: [3, 5, 7], row 3: [4, 9, 2].

chapters.chapter_title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

mind_map.root_topic: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

details: Three pairwise intersecting lines form a triangle.
A triangle can exist if and only if the sum of any two side lengths is strictly greater than the third side: a + b > c, b + c > a, c + a > b.
Shortcut test: Sum of the two smallest sides must strictly exceed the longest side.
evidence_or_examples: Sides 5, 10, 12: 5 + 10 = 15 > 12 (Triangle Exists).
Sides 3, 3, 7: 3 + 3 = 6 < 7 (No Triangle Exists).

details: Equilateral: All 3 sides equal (a = b = c). Always constructible for any s > 0 because s + s = 2s > s.
Isosceles: 2 sides equal (a = b != c).
Scalene: All 3 sides unequal (a != b != c).
evidence_or_examples: Equilateral triangle with sides 50 cm, 50 cm, 50 cm; Scalene triangle with sides 24 cm, 26 cm, 28 cm.

details: To multiply fractions, multiply numerators together and denominators together: (a / b) * (c / d) = (a * c) / (b * d).
evidence_or_examples: (2/3) * (4/5) = 8/15; Area model with 3/4 x 2/3 overlapping grid = 6/12 = 1/2.

details: Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: (a / b) / (c / d) = (a / b) * (d / c).
Dividing a whole number by a proper fraction (< 1) enlarges the quotient value.
evidence_or_examples: Maria decorating bags: 8 m / (1/4 m per bag) = 8 * 4 = 32 bags.
Water tank tap filling rate: 1 hr fills 7/10 => full tank time = 1 / (7/10) = 10/7 hours.

details: In products of the form (1 - 1/2)(1 - 1/3)(1 - 1/4)...(1 - 1/n), adjacent numerators and denominators cancel out completely.
The simplified product equals 1 / n.
